outcome: Give hotel gm / hospitality revenue director a governed method to improve late-ready rooms at check-in using checkout timestamps, room inspections and staffing rosters, with final decisions retained…
overview: Housekeeping Turnaround Forecasting addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in hospitality and tourism operations. The first proof of value uses checkout timestamps, room inspections and staffing rosters. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is late-ready rooms at check-in, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: checkout timestamps, room inspections and staffing rosters; define late-ready rooms at check-in and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hotel GM / Hospitality Revenue Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for late-ready rooms at check-in
